name: stata-research-guard
description: Stata command evidence and research authoring guidance with proportionate peer review.

interface.shortDescription: Stata 18 help-first command and research context.
interface.longDescription: Provides official or maintainer Stata command help and selected paper context. Research choices remain with the model and user. Peer review supports large data construction, complex specification changes, or explicit requests; no automatic review gate or startup hook.
defaultPrompt: Read the general rules once for the relevant Stata task, and revisit affected sections when the scope or rules change. Compare the actual research code and proposed call sites directly.
Use Phase 1 discovery only when the material command is unresolved; when it is already clear, call Phase 2 directly for the commands whose interface matters.

Do not call Guard for read-only explanation, comment or formatting-only edits, literal path or label changes with an unchanged command interface, verbatim relocation, or unchanged-file execution with no semantic issue.
When more context is needed, request expanded documentation only for the exact selected-command subset that needs it, and request exact paper blocks independently.

Do not turn a request to retain an existing analysis, robustness check, placebo, permutation, or export into a new mode, positional argument, dispatcher, or conditional branch unless that interface was explicitly requested or already required by the project.

Refactoring reduces indirection rather than lines. Repetition alone never authorizes a new program, ado, estimator or exporter wrapper, generic helper, or option-heavy interface; keep the estimator and exporter visible in the shallowest readable loop.
Treat paper examples and optional raw logs as nonbinding source context; preserve the current project and selected research specification.
Proceed from help when it fully explains the requested action and the code follows directly; report material help gaps and do not treat paper examples as grammar authority.
